extracted.intended_audience: FCC applicants (licensees/permittees/antenna registrants), Commission staff, SHPOs/THPOs, Indian tribes and Native Hawaiian organizations (NHOs)
extracted.subtask_description: Nationwide Programmatic Agreement guidance for when and how FCC Undertakings (tower/antenna Facilities) are subject to or excluded from Section 106 review, and the procedures Applicants, the Commission, SHPO/THPOs, tribes, NHOs, and the public must follow (identification, notification, consultation, submission packets, and assessment of effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and Scope of This Nationwide Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: This Nationwide Agreement (1) excludes from Section 106 review certain Undertakings involving the construction and modification of Facilities, and (2) streamlines and tailors the Section 106 review process for other Undertakings involving the construction and modification of Facilities. This Agreement applies only to federal Undertakings as determined by the Commission; the Commission has sole authority to determine what activities constitute Undertakings. Maintenance and servicing of Towers, Antennas, and associated equipment are not deemed Undertakings subject to Section 106 review. The Agreement does not apply to Antenna Collocations that are exempt under the Collocation Agreement, and does not apply on tribal lands except where a tribe elects to adopt the Agreement. It governs only review under Section 106 of the NHPA. Completion of the Section 106 review under this Agreement satisfies an Applicant's obligations under the Commission's rules with respect to Historic Properties except where an Undertaking has been determined to have an adverse effect requiring an Environmental Assessment. The Agreement does not govern Section 106 responsibilities of other federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative list of Commission activities covered is provided in Attachment 2. Collocations exempt under the Collocation Agreement are not submitted to SHPO/THPO. Where a tribe has assumed SHPO functions or elects to apply the Agreement on tribal lands, the term SHPO/THPO refers to the appropriate tribal or state official. Applicants must complete any other environmental reviews required for effects other than historic preservation (47 CFR 1.1301-1.1319).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Antenna
rubrics_metrics.description: An apparatus designed for the purpose of emitting radio frequency (“RF”) radiation, to be operated or operating from a fixed location pursuant to Commission authorization ... including the transmitting device and any on-site equipment, switches, wiring, cabling, power sources, shelters or cabinets associated with that antenna and added to a Tower, structure, or building as part of the original installation of the antenna. For most services, an Antenna will be mounted on or in, and is distinct from, a supporting structure such as a Tower, structure or building. For AM broadcast stations, the entire Tower or group of Towers constitutes the Antenna. The term Antenna does not include unintentional radiators, mobile stations, or devices authorized under Part 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: A Commission licensee, permittee, or registration holder, or an applicant or prospective applicant for a wireless or broadcast license, authorization or antenna structure registration, and the duly authorized agents, employees, and contractors of any such person or entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Area of Potential Effects (APE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The geographic area or areas within which an Undertaking may directly or indirectly cause alterations in the character or use of Historic Properties, if any such properties exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defining the APE is the first step in the Submission Packet and an essential basis for identifying Historic Properties and assessing effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Collocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The mounting or installation of an Antenna on an existing Tower, building, or structure for the purpose of transmitting radio frequency signals for telecommunications or broadcast purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Effect
rubrics_metrics.description: An alteration to the characteristics of a Historic Property qualifying it for inclusion in or eligibility for the National Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Experimental Authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorization issued to conduct experimentation utilizing radio waves for gathering scientific or technical operation data directed toward the improvement or extension of an established service and not intended for reception and use by the general public. Does not include an Experimental Broadcast Station under Part 74.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Facility / Tower
rubrics_metrics.description: Facility: A Tower or an Antenna. The term Facility may also refer to a Tower and its associated Antenna(s). Tower: Any structure built for the sole or primary purpose of supporting Commission-licensed or authorized Antennas, including the on-site fencing, equipment, switches, wiring, cabling, power sources, shelters, or cabinets associated with that Tower but not installed as part of an Antenna as defined herein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Field Survey
rubrics_metrics.description: A research strategy that utilizes one or more visits to the area where construction is proposed as a means of identifying Historic Properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Historic Property
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prehistoric or historic district, site, building, structure, or object included in, or eligible for inclusion in, the National Register maintained by the Secretary of the Interior. Includes artifacts, records, and remains related to and located within such properties, and properties of traditional religious and cultural importance to an Indian tribe or NHO that meet the National Register criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — National Register
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Register of Historic Places, maintained by the Secretary of the Interior's office of the Keeper of the National Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — SHPO/THPO Inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of records of previously gathered information, authorized by state or tribal law, on the absence, presence and significance of historic and archaeological resources within the state or tribal land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Special Temporary Authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization granted to a permittee or licensee to allow the operation of a station for a limited period at a specified variance from the terms of the station's permanent authorization or requirements of the Commission's rules applicable to the particular class or type of station.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Submission Packet (FCC Form 620/621)
rubrics_metrics.description: The document to be submitted initially to the SHPO/THPO to facilitate review of the Applicant's findings and any determinations with regard to the potential impact of the proposed Undertaking on Historic Properties in the APE. There are two Submission Packets: (a) The New Tower Submission Packet (FCC Form 620) and (b) The Collocation Submission Packet (FCC Form 621). Any documents required to be submitted along with a Form are part of the Submission Packet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission Packet contents and timing are prescribed in Section VII and Attachments 3 and 4. Consulting parties and SHPO/THPO receive copies as part of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — For time calculations and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: For the calculation of time periods under this Agreement, “days” mean “calendar days.” Any time period specified that ends on a weekend or a Federal or State holiday is extended until the close of the following business day. Written communications include communications by e-mail or facsimile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from Section 106 Review — Enhancement of a tower
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhancement of a tower and any associated excavation that does not involve a collocation and does not substantially increase the size of the existing tower, as defined in the Collocation Agreement. For towers constructed after March 16, 2001, this exclusion applies only if the tower has completed the Section 106 review process and any associated environmental reviews required by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination that an exclusion applies should be made by an authorized individual within the Applicant's organization, and Applicants should retain documentation of their determination. Concerns about application of exclusions may be presented to the Commission under Section XI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from Section 106 Review — Replacement towers without substantial increase
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction of a replacement for an existing communications tower and any associated excavation that does not substantially increase the size of the existing tower under elements 1-3 of the Collocation Agreement definition and that does not expand the boundaries of the leased or owned property surrounding the tower by more than 30 feet in any direction or involve excavation outside these expanded boundaries or outside any existing access or utility easement related to the site. For towers constructed after March 16, 2001, applies only if tower has completed prior Section 106 and environmental reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from Section 106 Review — Temporary Facilities (<=24 months except national security)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction of any temporary communications Tower, Antenna structure, or related Facility that involves no excavation or where all areas to be excavated are in areas described in VI.D.2.c.i, including but not limited to STAs, COWs, broadcast auxiliary services trucks, temporary ballast mount Towers, experimental authorization facilities. “Temporary” means for no more than twenty-four months duration except for Facilities associated with national security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from Section 106 Review — Small Facilities in large commercial/industrial centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction of a Facility less than 200 feet in overall height above ground level in an existing industrial park, commercial strip mall, or shopping center occupying total land area of 100,000 square feet or more, provided the park/strip mall/shopping center is not within the boundaries of or within 500 feet of a Historic Property as identified after a preliminary records search. Proposed Facilities within this exclusion must complete the process of participation of Indian tribes and NHOs pursuant to Section IV; if a Historic Property is identified during that process, Section 106 review must be completed notwithstanding the exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from Section 106 Review — Facilities in designated rights-of-way
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction of a Facility in or within 50 feet of the outer boundary of a right-of-way designated by a Federal, State, local, or Tribal government for location of communications Towers or above-ground utility transmission or distribution lines and associated structures and equipment and in active use for such purposes, provided (1) the proposed Facility would not constitute a substantial increase in size over existing structures in the right-of-way under Collocation Agreement elements 1-3, and (2) the proposed Facility would not be located within the boundaries of a Historic Property as identified after a preliminary search. Applicants must still complete tribal/NHO participation under Section IV and complete Section 106 review if a Historic Property is identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from Section 106 Review — SHPO/THPO designated low-potential areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction of a Facility in any area previously designated by the SHPO/THPO, at its discretion following consultation with appropriate Indian tribes and NHOs, as having limited potential to affect Historic Properties. Such designation must be documented by the SHPO/THPO and made available for public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable and good faith efforts to identify Indian tribes and NHOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants shall use reasonable and good faith efforts to identify any Indian tribe or NHO that may attach religious and cultural significance to Historic Properties that may be affected by an Undertaking. Reference to the Tower Construction Notification System constitutes a reasonable and good faith effort with respect to tribes/NHOs that have provided information there. Such efforts may include seeking information from SHPO/THPO, Indian tribes, state agencies, the U.S. BIA, or federal agencies with land holdings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting BIA, SHPO or other agencies is not a substitute for seeking information directly from Indian tribes. Applicants should consider ancestral, aboriginal, or ceded lands when identifying tribes/NHOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial contact responsibilities with Indian tribes/NHOs
rubrics_metrics.description: After identifying tribes/NHOs that may attach religious and cultural significance, the Commission has responsibility and the Applicant has obligation to ensure contact is made at an early planning stage to ascertain whether Historic Properties may be affected. Initial contact shall be made by the Commission or the Applicant, in accordance with the wishes of the tribe or NHO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Means of initial contact may include: electronic notification through the Tower Construction Notification System; written communication from the Commission at the Applicant's request; written, e-mail, or telephonic notification directly from the Applicant; any other means the tribe/NHO has informed the Commission are acceptable; or any means mutually agreed under Section IV.K. Initial contact is only the first step and does not substitute for government-to-government consultation unless the tribe/NHO disclaims further interest or agrees initial contact is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission's role in ascertaining tribal/NHO preferences and locations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will use its best efforts to ascertain the preferences of each Indian tribe and NHO for initial contact and to make these preferences available to Applicants, and to make available any locations or types of construction projects for which a tribe or NHO does not expect notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission encourages tribes/NHOs to accept the Tower Construction Notification System as an efficient means of making initial contact where comfortable.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Applicant may make initial contact directly
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of any contrary indication of a tribe/NHO's preference, where an Applicant has no pre-existing relationship with a tribe/NHO, initial contact shall be made through the Commission (possibly via Tower Construction Notification System). An Applicant with a pre-existing relationship shall make initial contact in the customary manner for that relationship. Applicants shall copy the Commission on initial written or electronic direct contact unless the tribe/NHO has agreed copying is not necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for sensitive and respectful direct contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants' direct contacts, where accepted by a tribe/NHO, shall be made in a sensitive manner consistent with reasonable wishes of the tribe/NHO. In general, unless guidance provided otherwise, Applicants shall: (1) be respectful of tribal sovereignty; (2) direct communications to the appropriate representative; (3) provide all information reasonably necessary for the tribe/NHO to evaluate whether Historic Properties may be affected (full information as early as reasonable); (4) ensure tribes/NHOs have a reasonable opportunity to respond (ordinarily 30 days); and (5) not assume failure to respond to a single communication means no interest — make reasonable follow-up efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where initial contact is automatic via the Tower Construction Notification System and a tribe/NHO has stated disinterest for particular types/locations, Applicant need not await a response for contacts meeting that description. If a tribe/NHO requests more time to respond, Applicant should afford additional time as reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes of communications with tribes/NHOs and referral to Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The purposes are (1) to ascertain whether Historic Properties of religious and cultural significance to the tribe/NHO may be affected and consultation is necessary, and (2) where possible and with concurrence, to reach agreement on presence/absence of effects that may obviate need for consultation. Applicants shall promptly refer to the Commission any request from a federally recognized tribe for government-to-government consultation. Applicants shall seek Commission guidance in cases of substantive or procedural disagreement or non-response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly advised to seek Commission guidance in cases of doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to tribes/NHOs to become consulting parties
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Indian tribe or NHO indicates a Historic Property of religious and cultural significance to it may be affected, the Applicant shall invite the commenting tribe/organization to become a consulting party. If it agrees, it shall be afforded that status and provided all the information and prerogatives of a consulting party as provided in 36 CFR 800.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of tribal information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information regarding Historic Properties to which tribes/NHOs attach religious and cultural significance may be highly confidential, private, and sensitive. If a tribe/NHO requests confidentiality from the Applicant, the Applicant shall honor it and shall request confidential treatment of such materials or information in accordance with the Commission's rules and Section 304 of the NHPA when submitting to the Commission. The Commission shall provide such confidential treatment consistent with its rules and applicable federal laws but cannot guarantee protection from disclosure under all circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices agreements with tribes/NHOs
rubrics_metrics.description: To promote efficiency and minimize misunderstandings, the Commission will use best efforts to arrive at agreements regarding best practices with tribes/NHOs and their representatives. Such best practices may include means of making initial contacts and guidelines for subsequent discussions. Where best practices exist, the Commission encourages Applicants to follow them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will strive for consistency among best practice agreements to the extent possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-existing arrangements between Applicants and tribes/NHOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing prohibits or limits Applicants and tribes/NHOs from entering into or continuing pre-existing arrangements governing their contacts, provided such arrangements are consistent with federal law and do not modify roles of other parties without their consent. Documentation of such alternative arrangements should be filed with the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local government notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: On or before the date an Applicant submits the appropriate Submission Packet to the SHPO/THPO, the Applicant shall provide the local government that has primary land use jurisdiction over the site with written notification of the planned Undertaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: On or before the date an Applicant submits the appropriate Submission Packet to the SHPO/THPO, the Applicant shall provide written notice to the public of the planned Undertaking. Notice may be accomplished through local zoning/historic preservation public notification provisions, publication in a local newspaper of general circulation, or other appropriate means including seeking assistance of local government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in written notice to local government and public
rubrics_metrics.description: The written notice shall include: (1) the location of the proposed Facility including its street address; (2) a description of the proposed Facility including its height and type of structure; (3) instruction on how to submit comments regarding potential effects on Historic Properties; and (4) the name, address, and telephone number of a contact person.

rubrics_metrics.name: SHPO/THPO lists of other groups to notify
rubrics_metrics.description: A SHPO/THPO may make available lists of other groups, including Indian tribes, NHOs and organizations of Indian tribes or NHOs, which should be provided notice for Undertakings located in particular areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of public comments received by Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Applicant receives a comment regarding potentially affected Historic Properties, the Applicant shall consider the comment and either include it in the initial submission to the SHPO/THPO, or, if the initial submission has already been made, immediately forward the comment to the SHPO/THPO for review. An Applicant need not submit to the SHPO/THPO any comment that does not substantially relate to potentially affected Historic Properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be consulting parties and how to determine status
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevant SHPO/THPO, Indian tribes and NHOs that attach religious and cultural significance to Historic Properties that may be affected, and the local government are entitled to be consulting parties. The Council may enter the Section 106 process on Commission invitation or on its own. An Applicant shall consider all written requests of other individuals and organizations to participate as consulting parties and determine which should be consulting parties, and is encouraged to grant status to those with a demonstrated legal or economic interest in the Undertaking or demonstrated expertise/standing as a representative of local or public interest in historic or cultural resources preservation. Any denial of consulting party status may be petitioned to the Commission. Applicants may seek Commission assistance in identifying and involving consulting parties. All entities granted consulting party status shall be identified to the SHPO/THPO as part of the Submission Packet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consulting parties' entitlements
rubrics_metrics.description: Consulting parties are entitled to (1) receive notices, copies of submission packets, correspondence and other documents provided to the SHPO/THPO in a Section 106 review; and (2) be provided an opportunity to have their views expressed and taken into account by the Applicant, the SHPO/THPO and, where appropriate, by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification, Evaluation, and Assessment of Effects — Required Steps
rubrics_metrics.description: In preparing the Submission Packet for the SHPO/THPO and consulting parties the Applicant shall: (1) Define the area of potential effects (APE); (2) identify Historic Properties within the APE; (3) evaluate the historic significance of identified properties as appropriate; and (4) assess the effects of the Undertaking on Historic Properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four tasks form the core of the Applicant's analysis in the Submission Packet and drive whether further consultation or mitigation is required.
